rows.effect: 11/11 inbound slots attacker; 11/11 honest rejected full
rows.rationale: 11 of 11 inbound slots go to the attacker; all 11 honest peers are rejected full.
rows.title: Multi-IP Sybil flood: 40 distinct-IP attackers fill inbound slots before honest peers arrive

rows.rationale: 10 of 10 outbound slots go to the attacker; 0 honest outbound peers.
rows.title: Eclipse isolation: poisoned livecache/bootcache steer all 10 outbound slots to attacker peers

rows.effect: 240/240 attempts wasted; 0 honest peers in 120 s
rows.rationale: 240 of 240 attempts wasted on dead endpoints; 0 honest peers in 120 s. Self-healing: the 300 dead endpoints are exhausted after 15 batches (~150 s), so the delay is bounded, not permanent.
rows.title: Attempt exhaustion: 300 dead endpoints in the bootcache burn autoconnect batches

rows.effect: 6 reserved peers activate; total active 27 (21 public + 6 reserved)
rows.rationale: 6 of 6 reserved peers activate while all 21 public slots are full. By design (fixed/cluster peers do not count toward limits); the exposure is configuration trust, not a control failure.
rows.title: Fixed/cluster bypass: 6 reserved peers activate while all 21 public slots are full

rows.effect: 22 of 200 endpoints cached; 178 dropped (136 truncated, 27 hops, 11 invalid, 4 duplicate)
rows.rationale: 22 of 200 gossiped endpoints enter the caches (livecache + bootcache); 178 are dropped by truncation, hops, invalid and duplicate filters. The 22 survivors are the seed for the S7 eclipse.
rows.title: Endpoint-gossip poisoning: one peer sends 200 endpoints (hops, invalid, duplicate, valid mix)

rows.effect: 36 churn events; 25 outbound refills within one batch; max outbound deficit 0; inbound drains 11 to 0
rows.rationale: Outbound availability loss is 0%: every dropped outbound peer is refilled within one batch and the node spends 0 ms below full outbound. The MEDIUM rating is for the asymmetry the run exposes: autoconnect never refills INBOUND slots, so inbound active drains 11 to 0 over 12 epochs. In a live network new peers dial in (which this scenario does not model), so the drain is a measured asymmetry, not a demonstrated outage.
rows.title: Peer churn: 3 of 21 peers drop every 10 s for 12 epochs; autoconnect refills

rows.effect: 30 of 50 redirects accepted; 20 rejected at cap
rows.rationale: 30 of 50 redirects accepted; the cap stops the remaining 20, so the attacker's goal of unbounded abuse is not achieved.
rows.title: Redirect abuse: one peer requests 50 redirects (maxRedirects 30)

rows.effect: 11 slots filled by 20 reused keys; 60 handshake rejects; 66 duplicate-key rejects; 63 slots-full rejects
rows.rationale: 11 of 200 attempts activate (the 11 inbound slots); 66 repeat attempts are rejected as duplicate keys, 63 more as slots full.
rows.title: Duplicate-identity flood: 200 inbound attempts reusing 20 keys, plus 60 bad handshakes

rows.rationale: 2 of 50 attempts activate (ipLimit 2); the flood is contained to 2 slots.
rows.title: Single-IP inbound flood: 50 attempts from one public IP (ipLimit 2)

rows.effect: 21/21 slots active (10 out + 11 in); 9 overshoot attempts rejected full
rows.rationale: Baseline fills all 21 slots; no attack present.
rows.title: Baseline: healthy mesh, 30 honest peers, full 21-peer slot table

rows.effect: first peer 100 ms; full outbound 10,100 ms; 40 endpoints learned from 4 hosts
rows.rationale: Cold start reaches full outbound in 10.1 s; no attack present.
rows.title: Bootstrap discovery: cold start from the 4 default bootstrap hosts
